---
title: "Find Similar iBGCs"
subtitle: "Expand your search around a cluster you like"
---

**Find similar iBGCs** takes one iBGC and finds the clusters across the catalogue that are most like it. It is the fastest way to go from a single good candidate to its relatives — and to check whether that candidate sits in a crowded family or stands alone.

## Running it

Right-click any iBGC — in the [roster](bgc-roster.qmd), on a [map](umap.qmd), or in a [detail panel](ibgc-detail.qmd) — and choose **Find similar iBGCs**. Unlike the sequence and chemical searches, it runs immediately; you do not press Run Query.

The results replace the current result set, ranked by similarity to the cluster you picked. The roster sorts by that similarity and its similarity column shows the score; on the [Variables map](variables-map.qmd) you can plot **Query similarity** on an axis.

## What "similar" means here

Similarity is measured from **shared protein domains and how they are arranged**, the same composite measure the platform uses for clustering and novelty — not from raw sequence. Two clusters rank as similar when they draw on the same domains in similar combinations, even if their sequences have diverged. (For a sequence-level search instead, use [Sequence Search](sequence-search.qmd).)

## How to use it

- **From a catalogue hit:** find one promising cluster, then find-similar to pull up its neighbours and judge how novel the family is. Many close hits → a populated family; few or none → an isolated, more novel cluster.
- **From your own data:** [load your assembly](load-asset.qmd), set one of your submitted iBGCs as the reference, and find-similar to retrieve the catalogue clusters most like it — a direct way to ask "what is my cluster closest to?"
- **Iteratively:** set a hit as the new reference and find-similar again to walk through a region of cluster space.
